best_for: Kubernetes engineers who switch between many clusters every day and want a desktop view of workloads, logs and metrics instead of long kubectl sessions.
description:
Lens K8S IDE is a desktop app for Kubernetes made by Mirantis. Mirantis says more than a million engineers use it. Nothing gets installed in your clusters: Lens runs on your computer with your kubeconfig and keeps to the permissions your RBAC rules give you.

It connects to any cluster with a Kubernetes API, from minikube and kind on your laptop to on-premises setups. Pin the clusters you use most to the hotbar for one-click access. Follow links from one resource to the ones it relates to, and keep logs next to the workload you are checking in split screens, tabs or separate windows. Watch cluster events as they arrive to catch restarts and scheduling failures, and add tools from the Extension Marketplace.

points.title: Clusters in one window
points.text: Lens lets you manage many clusters at once, browse resources, read live logs and metrics, open a terminal, forward ports, edit resources and manage Helm charts from a desktop app.

points.title: Free only for smaller users
points.text: The Personal plan is free for students, hobbyists and engineers at small organizations. Companies with more than USD 10 million in yearly revenue or funding need a paid plan after a 30-day evaluation.

points.title: What the paid plans add
points.text: Plus is USD 30 per month, or USD 180 for the first year when paid yearly, and adds AI help, GitOps with Flux or Argo CD, EKS, AKS and GKE links, and CVE reports. Pro is USD 25 per seat per month billed yearly and Enterprise USD 50, adding team management, SSO and air-gapped use. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: A Lens ID is required
points.text: The app has to be activated at first launch with a Lens ID, which you can create with an email address or a GitHub or Google sign-in. Offline activation for air-gapped networks is an Enterprise feature.

points.title: Kubeconfigs stay local
points.text: Lens says the Lens ID holds only basic profile data, and kubeconfigs, secrets and config maps are not uploaded to its cloud.

points.title: Versions kept here
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 39 versions, with per-user and machine-wide installers. macOS has separate Intel and Apple Silicon builds needing macOS 13 or later, and lists only the current release. Lens offers Linux builds, but this site does not list them.
